`pm:queue` → `pm:dispatched`. **Highest severity in the lane this round** (`priority:p1` + `security`).

---

## Zone 1 — BINDING. ⛔ NOT re-adjudicable.

**1.1 — The card's three non-claims are binding on you too. ⛔ Do not widen the card into them.**

- ⛔ **`isSystem: true` elevation is NOT the defect.** It is settled design (#3914's close-out was precisely to give an action body a writable context). This card says only that *after* elevation, the most natural authorization predicate the platform hands a handler is broken.
- ⛔ **Do NOT delete the `:1288` stamp.** New-record / record-less actions legitimately depend on `recordId` being in place. The defect is the **overlap** between "stamp condition" and "load-failed condition", not the stamp.
- ⛔ **Do NOT claim exploitation.** No exploitability work was done and none is asked for. This is a **predicate defect**, not an incident report. Keep that distinction in the PR body.

**1.2 — Direction 1 (additive) is the ruled route; direction 2 is NOT yours to take.**

The card names two directions. Direction 1 — give the handler an explicit signal that the caller-scope load was refused (e.g. a `ctx.recordLoadDenied`, or leave `ctx.record` `undefined` rather than stamping an id onto it) — is **additive** and is what you implement. Direction 2 — have the platform refuse before dispatch — **narrows the accept set of a published path** (today such a call reaches the handler).

⚠️ **If you conclude direction 1 is not viable and only direction 2 is: STOP and report the fork. ⛔ Do not narrow on your own authority.** This lane shipped a wrong narrowing ruling one round ago and the maintainer struck it; I am not repeating that shape. A fork report is the correct, expected deliverable here — not a failure.

**1.3 — Half of this defect is that it is undocumented. Fix that half in the same PR.** Whatever signal you add must be written into the action-authoring documentation. A correct mechanism nobody is told about leaves the reporter's complaint — *"every app author, human or AI, has to rediscover it or ship an authorization hole"* — standing.

---

## Zone 2 — PM mechanism assumptions. ⚠️ MEASURE. Falsification welcome.

**2.1 — I assume the triage seat's anchors have drifted.** They were taken on `origin/main` = `20b79bea`; the tree is now `1403d943`. The mechanism was still present when I checked — `packages/runtime/src/action-execution.ts:1285` carries the comment `/* new-record / record-less actions pass an empty record */` and **`:1288`** carries

```ts
if (record && (record as any).id == null && recordId) (record as any).id = recordId;
```

— but **re-derive `:1117`, `:1282`, `:1283` yourself** and take the tree's numbers over mine.

**2.2 — I assume the `catch` at `:1284` cannot today distinguish "refused" from "absent".** That is the whole mechanism, and it is the thing to measure first: does the caught error carry anything (a code, a class, a status) that already separates an authorization refusal from a genuinely missing row? ⭐ **If it does, the repair is much smaller than the card assumes** — say so, that is a good finding.

**2.3 — I assume this does NOT collide with #7401.** That card ("the write-by-id pre-image door resolves the row in the caller's scope, so an app-authored widening is still dead on `private`") is the same *pattern* — resolving a row in the caller's scope — pointed the opposite way: there the thing that **should** pass doesn't; here the thing that **shouldn't** pass does. Different site (`action-execution.ts` vs the write-by-id pre-image door). ⚠️ If your repair touches #7401's site, **stop and report** — they would then need one design, not two.

**2.4 — I assume `packages/runtime/src/action-execution.ts` is not claimed by any other in-flight seat.** Measured against the 10 open PRs at dispatch: none touches it. ⚠️ **A file-overlap reading has a shelf life measured in merges.** Re-check before you push; if another PR has since claimed it, stop and report rather than racing.

---

## Zone 3 — advisory. ⛔ Not binding.

The card's own framing is the sharpest available: today "the load failed" and "there was never a record" are **the same shape** on `ctx.record`. Anything that makes those two distinguishable at the handler boundary satisfies the card. Leaving `ctx.record` `undefined` on refusal is the smaller change but may break a handler that reads `ctx.record.someField` defensively; an added explicit flag is additive but only helps an author who knows to read it — which is why 1.3 is binding.

## STOP conditions

1. Only direction 2 (pre-dispatch refusal) works ⇒ **report the fork, do not narrow**.
2. The repair reaches #7401's site ⇒ report.
3. Another open PR has claimed `action-execution.ts` since dispatch ⇒ report.
4. `packages/spec` turns out to be in your diff ⇒ Clause ② **path limb** fires ⇒ declare it and say so up front.

## Verification expected

A test proving the predicate is now real: a caller who **cannot read** the row reaches the handler with a distinguishable signal, and a **new-record / record-less action still gets its `recordId`** (the regression the 1.1 prohibition exists to prevent). Both directions pinned. A firing positive control on any zero. The documentation change in the same PR. Plus a changeset, push, and a DRAFT PR saying `Closes #14143`.

⛔ Report anything unmeasured as **NOT MEASURED**. ⛔ No test skipped, disabled, quarantined or re-baselined. ⛔ Never `git stash`. ⛔ Never edit `content/docs/releases/`. Worktree-first.

Clause-②: yes — widens the public surface: a new `ctx.recordLoadDenied` key on the action context and on `ScriptContext`, documented to app authors. Path limb: no (`packages/spec` untouched).
